issues.summary: [Slice 2] Shopping List MVP
issues.description:
Objective: Implement the first usable household-scoped shopping-list workflow independently of pantry inventory, preserving Slice 1.1 authentication/authorization/data isolation.

Repository baseline: main 2e2535057efd7b71af56be120bbff4aff73bf8f9 (Expo SDK 58, Supabase migrations 00001–00003). Follow current pantry-flow/ implementation, not the legacy frontend/ scaffold or historical greenfield descriptions. Preserve Slice 1.1 and keep pending email-confirmation PR #3 as a separate release gate.

Architecture: reuse lib/supabase.ts, lib/auth.tsx, components/AuthGate.tsx, hooks/useHousehold.ts, shared-provider/mutation patterns in hooks/usePantryItems.tsx and hooks/useItemMutation.ts, existing membership-based RLS/column grants in migrations 00001–00003, theme/i18n/components and the Node/RNTL/pgTAP/local API/Maestro harness. No shopping table/provider/screen exists yet.

Acceptance criteria:
- Members can view, create, edit, complete, reopen and remove shopping items. Completed items remain recoverable; the latest brief supersedes historical removal-on-check examples.
- Households are isolated and unauthorized database/API access is rejected, including optional cross-household pantry links.
- Input/duplicate/reopen semantics are explicitly agreed and enforced consistently in UI/data/DB, including concurrent operations. Pantry strict uniqueness remains unchanged.
- Observable user journeys, state races, data invariants and native Android E2E pass without Slice 1.1 regressions.
- Physical release evidence and remaining independent production gates are reported accurately.

Implementation sequence: T1 model/database; T2 operations; T3 UI; T4 pantry integration; T5 final validation. T5 matrix/fixtures and T3 design can start earlier; do not serialize independent design/test work.

Out of scope: No custom backend, new auth/authorization framework, realtime service, offline queue, push notifications, AI/barcode/price features, quantity/expiry/batch expansion, invitations, premium gating or multi-household UX. Do not redesign existing screens.

This backlog task does not implement application code or apply migrations.

issues.summary: [Slice 2] Shopping List Domain Model and Database
issues.description:
Objective: Establish shopping-list persistence using existing Supabase/PostgreSQL conventions.

Implementation context and reuse: Use pantry_households and pantry_household_members from pantry-flow/supabase/migrations/00001_first_slice.sql. Apply 00002_review_hardening.sql column-grant, auth.uid attribution and server-timestamp conventions; preserve 00003_strict_duplicate_prevention.sql pantry invariants. docs/A_PantryFlow_PRD.md proposes pantry_shopping_items but no shopping table exists today.

Scope: Produce the minimal shopping model and the next version-controlled migration after 00003. Record approved duplicate/completed/reopen semantics first. Reuse membership-based RLS SQL patterns; there is no existing generic authorization service to replace.

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema and migration are reviewed/version-controlled without rewriting migrations 00001–00003.
- Membership and optional pantry-link household consistency are enforced in PostgreSQL, not just the client.
- Ordinary users and anonymous clients cannot access another household or forge creators/ownership/timestamps.
- Blank/invalid records fail; concurrent inserts/renames/reopens preserve the explicitly approved uniqueness contract.
- Completion remains reopenable until explicit deletion; shopping deletion/completion never changes pantry state.

Dependencies and parallel work: First implementation task; product/data decisions precede migration. Test design with T5 can start immediately.

Exclusions: No custom backend, new auth/authorization framework, realtime service, offline queue, push notifications, AI/barcode/price features, quantity/expiry/batch expansion, invitations, premium gating or multi-household UX. Do not redesign existing screens.

issues.summary: [Slice 2] Shopping List Operations
issues.description:
Objective: Implement shopping create/read/update/complete/reopen/delete through the existing client and state architecture.

Implementation context and reuse: Reuse pantry-flow/lib/supabase.ts, lib/auth.tsx and hooks/useHousehold.ts. Follow lib/pantry-data.ts validation/parsing/pagination patterns and hooks/usePantryItems.tsx identity-keyed provider, generation guards and per-item pending set. That data module is pantry-specific, not a generic CRUD repository.

Scope: Add a shopping-specific domain module/provider only as consumed by this slice. Share the existing household scope (expose its current householdId or narrowly extract shared ownership with regression tests), rather than invoking a second independent household lookup per screen. Keep business decisions out of UI handlers.

Acceptance criteria:
- All six operations persist and respect the authenticated household and approved domain contract.
- Validation and response parsing reject malformed data; reads do not truncate beyond server row caps.
- Appropriate translated keys map validation, permission, missing-record, duplicate and transport failures.
- Shared state updates all consumers; stale reads cannot undo mutations or repopulate a signed-out/changed household.
- Double-submit, competing item operations and abandoned requests fail/recover predictably; no offline success or backend service is invented.

Dependencies and parallel work: Depends on T1 schema/security contract. Operation interfaces and test design may proceed while T1 migration work is underway.

Exclusions: No custom backend, new auth/authorization framework, realtime service, offline queue, push notifications, AI/barcode/price features, quantity/expiry/batch expansion, invitations, premium gating or multi-household UX. Do not redesign existing screens.
